nine, and which are distant from one another by one palm: and in the middle circle, first write the name of the hour in which you perform the work; in the second place, the name of the Angel of the hour; thirdly, the seal <note>original: "sigillum"</note> of the Angel of the hour; fourthly, the name of the Angel who rules that day in which you perform the work, and his ministers; fifthly, the name of the present season <note>original: "temporis præfentis"</note>. Sixthly, the name of the Spirits reigning in that part of the season, and presiding over it. Seventhly, the name of the head of the sign <note>referring to the zodiacal sign</note> reigning in that part of the season in which you perform the work. Eighthly, the name of the Earth, according to that part of the season in which you perform the work. Ninthly, and for the completion of the middle circle, write the names of the Sun and Moon, according to the aforementioned calculation of the season. For when the Season is changed, the names also change. In the upper circle, however, let the names of the angels presiding over the air on that day in which you perform the work be assigned in the four corners: namely, the King and his three ministers. Outside the circle, let there be Pentagons in the four corners. In the lower circle, four Divine names should be written with crosses placed between them. <summary>This page details the specific inscriptions required for a magical circle, including planetary, angelic, and seasonal names. It explains how these names must be adjusted based on the timing of the ritual and the spirits being summoned.</summary>
